title: Hand-Hygiene and PPE Compliance Monitoring
summary: Measure hand-hygiene opportunities and PPE use at ICU, ward and OT entry points from cameras, with faces blurred on the device and results shown as unit-level trends for infection control.

seo.title: Hand-Hygiene and PPE Monitoring with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Privacy-first computer vision for infection control: dispenser use at patient-zone entry and PPE at OT and isolation doors, reported as unit-level trends.

problem.intro: Infection control teams audit hand hygiene and PPE by direct observation, a few sessions a month per unit. Staff behave differently when an auditor is watching, and the samples are too small to show patterns by shift or location. The infection control committee still needs evidence to target training, dispensers and supplies.

pain_points.title: Small observation samples
pain_points.detail: Manual audits cover a small fraction of opportunities, mostly during day shifts.

pain_points.title: Observer effect
pain_points.detail: Compliance rises while the auditor is present and falls once they leave.

pain_points.title: PPE lapses at critical points
pain_points.detail: Missing masks, caps or gowns at OT and isolation room entry are noticed only when someone happens to see them.

pain_points.title: Valid privacy concerns
pain_points.detail: Cameras in clinical areas worry staff and patients, so any system must be designed for privacy from the start.

solution.overview: We build a computer vision system that watches defined points such as ICU bed-zone entries, isolation room doors, sanitiser dispensers and OT entrances. It detects events that stand in for hand-hygiene opportunities, such as entering a patient zone, and whether a dispenser was used within a set window, and it checks visible PPE such as masks, caps, gowns and gloves where policy requires them. Processing runs on an edge device inside the hospital. Faces are blurred before anything is stored, and only event data and short blurred clips for audit leave the device. Infection control sees compliance trends by unit, shift and location, not a ranking of individuals.
capabilities: Zone-entry and dispenser-use event detection at agreed points
PPE detection for masks, caps, gowns and gloves at OT and isolation entries
Edge processing with face blurring before any storage
Compliance trends by unit, shift and location for infection control
Optional real-time reminder at OT doors, such as a light or chime
Sampled blurred clips for auditors to verify detection quality

workflow.title: Agree points and rules
workflow.detail: Infection control and nursing leads choose camera points and define rules, such as dispenser use before entering a bed zone.

workflow.title: Detect on the edge
workflow.detail: Edge devices detect zone entries, dispenser use and visible PPE in real time.

workflow.title: Anonymise
workflow.detail: Faces are blurred and no identity data is stored; only events and blurred audit clips are kept.

workflow.title: Check confidence
workflow.detail: Low-confidence events are left out of metrics or sampled for auditor review.

workflow.title: Aggregate and report
workflow.detail: Events roll up into compliance trends by unit, shift and location on the infection control dashboard.

workflow.title: Act on findings
workflow.detail: The infection control committee reviews trends and decides on training, dispenser placement or supply changes.

inputs: Floor plans with bed zones, doors and dispenser locations
Hand-hygiene and PPE rules from the infection control policy
outputs: PPE compliance events at entry points
Compliance trends by unit, shift and location
Monthly report for the infection control committee
human_in_the_loop: Infection control auditors verify sampled events and calibrate the system against their own observations, and the committee decides on any action. The system reports at unit level and is not designed to identify individual staff.
integrations: Existing CCTV or video management system where angles allow
Edge devices on the hospital network
Hospital IT security and network policies
Optional door-side indicator lights or chimes
guardrails: Faces blurred on the edge device before any storage
No cameras pointed at beds, toilets, changing areas or exposed patients
Reporting at unit and shift level, never individual staff rankings
Signage and staff briefings before go-live
Short retention for clips, with access limited to infection control
compliance_notes: Video of staff and patients is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023, so notices, minimisation and short retention are built into the design.
Supports, but does not replace, the hand-hygiene audits used in infection control programmes and accreditation reviews such as NABH.

pilot.scope: One ICU or one OT complex with a small number of camera points, run alongside the infection control team's usual observation audits.
deliverables: Camera point plan and rules agreed with infection control
Comparison of system events with auditor observations
Privacy review notes and roll-out plan

what_we_measure.how: System events compared with simultaneous auditor observations at the same points.
Sampled clips reviewed by auditors for correct and missed PPE events.
Hours and shifts observed by the system compared with manual audit in the same period.
Feedback from staff briefings and any concerns raised during the pilot.

faqs.q: Can a camera really judge the WHO five moments for hand hygiene?
faqs.a: Not fully. Cameras see proxies, such as entering a patient zone and using a dispenser, and we are clear about that. The system adds coverage and trends to your audits; it does not replace trained observers.

faqs.q: Will it be used to discipline staff?
faqs.a: It is designed for unit-level trends, with faces blurred on the device. How results are used is your policy decision, and we recommend agreeing it with staff before go-live.

faqs.q: Can we use our existing CCTV?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Many CCTV cameras sit too high or at the wrong angle to see hands and dispensers. We survey the points first and recommend dedicated cameras only where needed.
No raw video leaves the edge device. Only anonymous events and short blurred clips go to the dashboard, which can run on your servers or in your cloud account.
